description: This Java source file defines an abstract class AbstractRealDistribution, serving as a base for probability distribution implementations on the real number line within Apache Commons Math library. It provides default implementations for common distribution functionalities such as probability calculations, inverse CDF, sampling, and handling of support bounds.

classes.name: AbstractRealDistribution
classes.description: An abstract class providing common implementations for real-valued probability distributions, including probability calculations, sampling, and inverse CDF methods, intended as a superclass for specific distribution implementations.

methods.name: cumulativeProbability
methods.description: Returns the probability of the distribution falling between two bounds, default implementation subtracts the CDF values and is deprecated.

methods.name: probability
methods.description: Calculates the probability that the distribution falls within a specified range [x0, x1], default implementation uses cumulative probability differences.

methods.name: inverseCumulativeProbability
methods.description: Computes the inverse of the cumulative distribution function (quantile) for a probability p, employing bracketing and root-finding techniques with optional bounds.

methods.name: getSolverAbsoluteAccuracy
methods.description: Returns the absolute accuracy used in inverse cumulative probability calculations.

methods.name: reseedRandomGenerator
methods.description: Resets the random number generator seed for reproducible sampling.

methods.name: sample
methods.description: Generates a random sample from the distribution using inverse transform sampling.

methods.name: sample (batch)
methods.description: Generates multiple samples from the distribution.

methods.name: probability (single)
methods.description: Returns the probability density function at a specific point, default is zero, meant to be overridden.

methods.name: logDensity
methods.description: Returns the logarithm of the probability density function at a point, uses density method.
